Indias Rishabh Pant (R) celebrates 100 runs with team mate Dhruv Jurel on November 22, 2026 | Photo Credit: AFP
Dhruv Jurel believes India’s bowlers have given themselves a chance of forcing a result in the first Test against New Zealand, despite a surface that has progressively slowed down and stayed low at Basin Reserve.
The wicketkeeper-batter, whose 78 provided the finishing touch to India’s mammoth 720/9 declared, reckons the visitors need to string together eight good deliveries to create the openings required to bowl New Zealand out on the final day.
“The wicket is getting slow, day by day. It is also staying a little low, so we just need to be lucky. We need to bowl eight good balls,” Jurel said after the penultimate day’s play on Sunday (November 22, 2026). “We were bowling according to our plans, and I think it’s turning out well for us.”
India’s preparation for the Test included three four-day matches against New Zealand A, with Jurel leading the side. However, the conditions during those games were different, and the wicketkeeper-batter felt the weather had a greater bearing on the surface at Basin Reserve than anticipated.
“The weather was different when we played for India A. But I have observed that the weather matters more than the wicket over here. If the weather was a little cloudy, there would have been something in the wicket too. It wasn’t expected that it would be sunny for three days and dry down,” he said.
Jurel’s contribution with the bat included a 75-run stand with Rishabh Pant, during which he watched his fellow wicketkeeper-batter reach a spectacular hundred. Pant’s audacious strokeplay eventually took him to 128 off 153 balls, with six sixes, as India extended its lead before declaring.
Jurel was also responsible for one of the moments of the day in the field, lunging forward at short-leg to pluck a bat-pad chance inches off the ground and dismiss first-innings centurion Henry Nicholls off Prasidh Krishna.
“You cannot really train for such catches, but it was fun. I am a wicketkeeper, so it makes a difference. You practice keeping drills and the reflexes are fast. You are used to reacting once you see the ball. Today I was fortunate that I caught it,” he said.
Jurel was equally effusive about Pant, whose unpredictability continues to leave even his teammates intrigued.
“He is a phenomenal player. The way he plays, I am always curious about his mindset. Whenever I speak to him, I always ask him, ‘What are your thoughts while batting?’” Jurel said.
“Suddenly, he steps out and hits the ball over covers or wherever, so he is some kind of player. I love him as a player, as a mentor. Whenever I talk to him, he always gives positive vibes.”
With Wellington’s wind expected to make an appearance on Monday, India will hope its bowlers can find enough assistance to turn Jurel’s ‘eight good balls’ into a match-winning sequence.
